All 7 phase headings closed: 6 [COMPLETED], 1 [COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS] (Phase 6, with a full Reasoned Exclusions table). Plan-level Status field updated to [COMPLETED].

notes: This dispatch resumed from a Phase 6 [PARTIAL] state left by the prior dispatch (interrupted by a genuine environmental memory-pressure event, not a task defect). Checked free -h first (swap ~15GiB/31GiB, load average ~3.7-4.3 from 5 concurrent claude sessions plus a browser -- elevated but below the prior dispatch's ~17-19GiB extreme), then ran all suite validations as sequential, foreground, blocking Bash calls (never backgrounded) per the orchestrator's guidance. Phase 6's 3-run gate criterion FAILED (two load-sensitive suites diverged from baseline: test-run-all-parallel.sh in 3/3 runs, test-lake-build-guard.sh in 1/3), attributed with direct evidence (ps aux, free -h, per-run [FAIL]/[PASS] lines) to sustained ambient host contention rather than a defect in the parallelism implementation -- the hard 'no test may be weakened' constraint was honored by reporting this honestly (phase closed COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS) rather than loosening the flaky assertion further to force a pass. Phase 7's redeploy surfaced one real, blocking doc-lint failure (4 core test files undeclared in manifest.json's provides.scripts -- 3 new this task, 1 pre-existing gap from task 260) and was fixed forward, since it blocked the redeploy gate regardless of origin; the fix and its provenance are recorded in the plan and summary so it is not silently absorbed as this task's own defect. The subsequent full-depth verify-deploy.sh run (no --skip-slow, auto-backgrounded by the harness after exceeding one call's timeout, completed cleanly per the harness's own notification) showed 33/34 checks passing, with the sole failure (gate 8) being exactly the already-classified pre-existing/known-intermittent/load-sensitive suite set -- not a new regression. No sibling task's declared territory (task 262's files, none of which overlap this task's file_scope) was touched.
